limitations: Discovery selects at most MaxSeeds eligible distinct masters plus actual query origin and distinct bootstrap seeds, total <=2*MaxSeeds+1. The constructor preallocates address/hash/plan storage and (MaxSeeds+1)*MaxHostBytes host arena (17KiB default), even with one initial seed. Per-host constructor costs are measured separately; metadata planning copies bounded hosts and scans the map.

Discovery itself allocates no storage and performs no policy/I/O; subsequent exact-address cache lookup still authorizes. Map/epoch/generation and retained outcomes are unchanged. Active/Busy phases reject discovery; close includes Busy. SHARDS selects explicit transport port and SOURCE uses copied query host; unknown/unhealthy/oversize/unavailable masters and replicas are ineligible.

The real-Cluster fault denies the original seed at the cache authorization gate, with identity-verified prewarmed pools retained for administration. It demonstrates discovered-endpoint refresh, not server-process death, replica failover, cold reconnect or full TLS/auth/trust recovery. TLS port selection is tested with parsed topology fixtures, not a new real TLS deployment.

Same-function unpinned serial closed-loop benchmark swaps only cluster_client and cluster_refresh objects against the recorded baseline. Common objects, benchmark, flags, peer/payload and queue semantics match. Setup/bootstrap/sample buffers are excluded from warm-loop throughput/tails; first-window costs and FIFO head-of-line effects remain. Cold storage is reported separately. No zero-overhead claim.

Native client/pool/cache/Core sources and layouts remain unchanged. Single footprint combines XRT/product; static/shared primary rows are product-only with adjacent Core artifacts inventoried separately. This does not establish new native-I/O performance.

WSL/local microbenchmarks do not establish native Linux/fixed-arrival/concurrent/mixed-load/upstream/CPU/RSS/72h acceptance. Noise/resolution-unqualified observations remain unqualified without rerun for green.
Replica policy, command-key metadata, synchronous Cluster facade and complete four-library production/performance acceptance remain open.
